conventions.convention: Coordinate permutations act by (τπz)i = zπ(i); exchangeability is invariance of the joint law under every such permutation.
Scores are real-valued, smaller scores are more conforming, and nonrandomized upper ranks count every score greater than or equal to the candidate, including the candidate.
Tie randomization uses an independent Lebesgue-uniform U on [0,1], multiplying the entire candidate tie-block size; one U is shared across the candidate scan.
For m ≥ 0 and 0 < α < 1, split conformal uses k = ceil((m+1)(1−α)), the kth calibration score when k ≤ m, and +∞ when k = m+1; ordinary membership is score ≤ threshold.
Full conformal and both randomized sets include a candidate exactly when its corresponding p-value is strictly greater than α.

Split coverage assumes a supplied regular conditional distribution of the entire calibration/test tuple with exchangeable sections almost surely, a training-measurable H, and jointly measurable score evaluation; randomized conditional coverage requires U independent of the training sigma-field joined with the data sigma-field.

load_bearing.statement: Let R₁,…,Rₙ be an exchangeable real random vector with n ≥ 1. Its last-coordinate upper-rank p-value pₙ = #{i ≤ n : Rᵢ ≥ Rₙ}/n satisfies P(pₙ ≤ u) ≤ u for every u ∈ [0,1]. If U is independent of R with Lebesgue probability law on [0,1], then (#{i ≤ n : Rᵢ > Rₙ} + U #{i ≤ n : Rᵢ = Rₙ})/n has the uniform law on [0,1].

Given a regular conditional distribution K of X given a sub-sigma-algebra G and a measurable g:(Ω,G)×(S,Σ)→(T,Τ), K_g(ω,B)=K(ω,{x:g(ω,x)∈B}) is a regular conditional distribution of g(ω,X(ω)) given G. If U has law λ and is independent of G joined with σ(X), then K(ω,·)⊗λ is a regular conditional distribution of (X,U) given G.
Let Z be an exchangeable random element of Z-space to the nth power, and let A into Rⁿ be measurable and permutation-equivariant. Then A(Z) is an exchangeable real random vector.

For measurable real-valued R₁,…,Rₘ with m ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ k ≤ m, the kth order statistic is measurable. The finite upper-rank p-value and tie-randomized rank with a measurable U on the same space are measurable.

For n ≥ 1 measurable spaces equipped with their finite product sigma-algebra, a tuple of measurable coordinate maps is measurable. When all factors are the same measurable space, every coordinate permutation is measurable.
